name: Fifty-one Chinese (Wǔshíyī Diǎn)
description: Fifty-one Chinese (Wǔshíyī diǎn / äº”å ä¸€ç‚¹) is a strategic collection game primarily played in the northern Fujian province of China. The game is centered around point-optimization within a single suit, where players attempt to assemble a hand of five cards of the same suit that totals as close to 51 points as possible. Unlike many Western card games, Fifty-one Chinese features a dynamic 'Table Exchange' mechanic where players can swap multiple cards at once with a public pool of facendup cards.

history.origins: Wǔshíyī diǎn is a regional specialty of the Nanping area in Fujian. It shares a common ancestor with the Japanese game '51', but has developed more complex exchange rules and scoring nuances.
timeline: Early 20th Century: Variations of '51' emerge across East Asia.
1950s-1980s: Wǔshíyī diǎn becomes a prominent social pastime in Nanping.
Modern Era: Continues to be played by locals as a quick, social 'pub' style card game.
history.cultural: Used as a common ice-breaker in Fujian social gatherings; emphasizes rapid decisionndmaking and public resource management.
history.evolution: The game's scoring (Aces as 11, Faces as 10) mirrors ancient European 'Points' games, suggesting a long history of cross-cultural adaptation from maritime trade routes reaching Fujian.

setup.players: Typically 4 players playing individually. 3 players is also common.
setup.dealing: Players draw cards from a face-down stack one by one. The starting player gets 6 cards; others get 5. The starter begins by discarding their sixth card to the table.

rules.objective: Collect 5 cards of the same suit with the highest possible total value. A perfect hand (Ace, King, Queen, Jack, Ten) equals 51 points.
rules.gameplay:
Turns proceed anticlockwise. On your turn, you must choose one of these actions:
1. Draw & Discard: Draw 1 card from the stock and discard 1 to the table.
2. Exchange One: Swap 1 card from your hand with 1 facendup card on the table.
3. Exchange All: Swap your entire 5ndcard hand for the 5 cards on the table.
4. Call: If your hand is all one suit, you may 'call' and end the round immediatey.
keyRules: Suit Matching: Only cards of the SAME suit in your hand contribute to your score. Mixedndsuit hands score only the value of the highest single suit within them.
Automatic Call: If you reach exactly 51 points, you win the round instantly.
Table Clear: If all 5 cards on the table are cleared, the next player must draw from the stock.

strategy.basic: Pick a suit early based on your starting hand and stick to it. Don't be afraid to exchange your whole hand if the table has 3 or 4 cards of a suit you can use.
strategy.intermediate: Deny your opponents: If you see someone collecting Hearts, and there is a Heart Ace on the table, take it even if you are collecting Spades. This prevents them from hitting 51.
strategy.advanced: Timing the Table Refresh: If the table is full of 'junk' cards, use the 'Draw & Discard' action to try and force a table clear, giving you a fresh set of facendup options on your next turn.
tips: Aces are the most valuable cards; always prioritize picking them up from the table.
If you 'Call', ensure you have at least 40 points; calling early with a weak 30-point hand often leads to an opponent beating you with a lategame draw.

scoring.description: Collect 5 cards of same suit totaling as close to 51 points as possible. Ace=11, K/Q/J=10, 2-10=face value. Perfect 51 wins instantly.
scoring.winCondition: Highest single-suit total (max 51). Exact 51 = automatic win.

synthesis.shortDescription: A Chinese collection game where players assemble 5 cards of the same suit totaling as close to 51 as possible using strategic exchanges.
